basics.name: Taha Ali
basics.label: Engineer · Researcher · Writer
basics.summary: Academic, researcher, consultant, and writer working at the intersection of computer networks, information security, emerging technologies, technology policy, and society.

work.name: National University of Sciences and Technology (NUST)
work.summary: I teach in the NUST School of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science (SEECS). I head the Cognet Lab, where we research security applications in new and emerging technologies, including blockchain, machine learning, computer vision, and Internet of Things.
highlights: Courses include computer programming, computer networks, network security, and cryptocurrencies.
Undergraduate teaching includes Fundamentals of ICT, Fundamentals of Programming, and Computer Networks.
Masters teaching includes Computer Networks, Network Routing and Switching, Advanced Computer Networks, Selected Topics in Networks, and Cryptocurrencies and Blockchain.
Introduced a Masters-level course on Cryptocurrencies and Blockchain technology at NUST in 2018.
25 Masters students and 2 PhD students have graduated under my supervision.
Usually receive student feedback in the >85% range.

work.name: National University of Sciences and Technology (NUST)
highlights: Taught courses in computer programming, computer networks, network security, and cryptocurrencies.
Developed research and teaching activities around computer networks, information security, blockchain, machine learning, computer vision, and Internet of Things.

work.name: Newcastle University
highlights: Worked on a flagship EU project on secure and verifiable electronic voting systems.
Contributed to projects on cryptocurrencies and blockchain.
Initiated a project on next-generation botnets.
Contributed to the book Real-World Electronic Voting: Design, Analysis and Deployment.

work.name: University of New South Wales
highlights: Worked on security and green applications of software-defined networks.
Researched data provenance mechanisms for healthcare and IoT devices.

work.name: CSIRO
highlights: Worked on a project to improve the energy efficiency of residential WiFi networks.
Developed algorithms to strategically adjust the mode and transmit power of WiFi access points in response to user traffic.
Achieved power savings of up to 40% in the project.
Showcased a working demonstration in June 2012.

work.name: WorldCALL Broadband, Pvt. Ltd.
highlights: Took on engineering and management roles in the Engineering department.
Worked on deployment of Pakistan's largest hybrid-fiber-coax broadband network.

education.thesis: Security Mechanisms for Body Sensor Networks
highlights: Supervisors: Vijay Sivaraman (UNSW), Diethelm Ostry (CSIRO).
Developed novel solutions for security requirements in bodyworn health monitoring devices, including secure broadcast, data confidentiality, data authentication, and provenance.
Developed efficient and lightweight security solutions for resource-constrained bodyworn devices, including the use of unorthodox non-crypto primitives.
Validated the work through extensive experimentation in indoor living and work spaces, experimental anechoic chambers, and outdoor settings.

education.institution: GIK Institute of Engineering Sciences & Technology
highlights: Final Year Project: Software Control for Embedded Systems using Jini.

projects.name: Coding Fellows Program
projects.summary: A two-year education project to train 75 teachers to deliver STEM education in coding, AI, IT, and information security across 150 government schools in Islamabad.
highlights: Developing and curating lesson plans.
Organizing STEM competitions and tournaments between schools.
Organizing introductory university visits for students.
Project funded by the Ministry of Education.

projects.name: High Impact Skills Development Program in AI, Data Science, and Blockchain
projects.summary: A flagship collaboration between the Gilgit Baltistan government and NUST focused on developing advanced technology skills and supporting the local IT and freelancing community.
highlights: Curating and teaching a six-month specialized blockchain technology course.
Course covers cryptocurrencies, smart contracts, Solidity essentials, decentralized applications, security, policy, and advanced topics.

projects.name: Electronic Voting Machines for Pakistan
projects.summary: RASTA research project to develop a policy framework and comprehensive roadmap for introducing electronic voting in Pakistan.
highlights: Served as Co-PI.
Project funded by the Pakistan Institute of Development Economics (PIDE) through its RASTA competitive grants program.
Project report: Electronic Voting Machines for Pakistan: Opportunities, Challenges, and the Way Forward.

projects.name: PIVOT – Promoting Innovative Voting Technologies
projects.summary: NUST research initiative promoting responsible use of election technology.
highlights: Involved technical talks, newspaper articles, a Twitter presence, and a dedicated newsletter.
Undertook the first study in Pakistan on the dynamics of overseas voting: The Game-Changing Overseas Vote.

volunteer.position: Research Consultant: Election Technologies and Best Practices
highlights: Authored concept notes and developed roadmaps for introducing electronic voting machines in Pakistan.
Assisted the Election Commission of Pakistan with plans to establish an in-house R&D Center.
Advised on modernization of processes, overseas voting, stakeholder outreach, staff training programs, and election monitoring strategies.
Liaised with research institutes, universities, and civil society groups to collaborate with the Election Commission of Pakistan.

volunteer.organization: Trust for Democratic Education and Accountability (TDEA)
volunteer.position: Consultant: Technology for Efficient and Effective Elections (T3E)
highlights: Worked on research and improvement of technology use in Pakistan's electoral processes.
Served as a member of the Election Tech Forum, a gathering of experts and civil society personnel providing technical expertise.
Served as Member of the President's Subcommittee on Emerging Technologies.
Served on committees for the Ministry of IT & Telecommunications and the Ministry of Science and Technology.
Advised a Parliamentary consultation on digital rights, assets, and cryptocurrency.
Served on the Election Commission's Technical Committee responsible for devising policy on electronic voting and assessing different electronic voting machines.
Co-curated the One Vote Annual Conference on Rights, Access, and Technology in Elections.
Delivered a talk titled How a State Examines Technology on Pakistan's election technology experience.
